terms.d: The DOTS we expect at the lifter's next full-power meet if it were held today: the last meet, adjusted for what the training years say about lifters at the same stage (meets so far, age, time away) and for how the last meet compares with their longer-run level and best.
A total adjusted for bodyweight (Konertz, 2019): total x 500 / a fourth-degree polynomial of bodyweight. Lets a 60 kg and a 120 kg lifter be compared on one scale.
The IPF's own bodyweight formula (Goodlift points, 2020), used for best-lifter awards at IPF meets.
The older bodyweight formula (Wilks, revised 2020); some federations still rank by it.
A ranking pool: men or women, raw (sleeves only), wraps (knee wraps allowed) or equipped (single-ply, multi-ply or unlimited suits and shirts).
The weight class from the bodyweight on the day, on the IPF's 2019 classes (men 59 to 120+ kg, women 47 to 84+ kg), whatever class the federation used.
Our pre-meet expected DOTS turned into kilos at the bodyweight on the day. Built only from meets before this one.
Actual DOTS minus our pre-meet expectation: how much better (or worse) than expected the lifter did.
How often the lifter finished in the top three of the flight (same meet, division, class and equipment) when we simulated the flight 400 times from our expectations, with the chance of bombing out.
A full-power meet without a total: three missed attempts on one lift (or a disqualification). OpenPowerlifting marks it DQ.
The share of attempts that counted. Each lifter gets three attempts per lift; misses are negative in the archive.
The step from a made second attempt to the third, as a share of the second.
Fewer than five scored meets behind a rating: read it with care.
A meet run under drug testing by the federation (OpenPowerlifting's Tested flag).

Where a lifter sits among the active lifters of the same stream and IPF class (two or more meets in two years): 90 means better than 90 in 100. For a lower-is-better metric the percentile is turned so higher is better; for a style (lift shares, jump size) it is only a position.
A personal record: a total above the lifter's best before this meet, in the same stream.
The years 2023 to 2025, scored once with a model fitted on 1990 to 2019 and chosen on 2020 to 2022.
